name: Throw playing cards accurately
blurb: A card thrown with enough spin flies flat, fast and surprisingly far. It is all in the grip and the wrist snap, and a cheap deck gives you 52 attempts per round.
gear: Cheap plastic-coated decks — you will destroy several
A target, and a lot of space
steps: Learn the grip: the card held between index and middle finger at one corner, curled back into the palm.
Learn the throw: the arm moves little, the wrist and forearm snap the card out with heavy spin.
Aim for spin first, distance second. A card without spin tumbles and drops within a metre.
Practise at a large target at three metres before trying to hit anything small.
Learn the horizontal and the vertical throw, which suit different targets.
Build up power gradually — a well-thrown card can travel 20 metres and does sting.
tips: Never throw at a person’s face. A hard-thrown card can cut skin and can certainly damage an eye.
A tumbling card means not enough spin, not a weak arm.
proof: You hit a target the size of a dinner plate at five metres, five throws out of ten.
